item.title: [IGNITE-2004] Asynchronous execution of ContinuousQuery's remote filter & local list
item.description:
Presently remote filters are executed synchronously an entry update. This leads to the limitation when it's disallowed to perform cache related operation in a filter body.

It's required to add the ability to execute remote filters asynchronously. This will let to execute any kind of operations including cache operations directly in the filter body.

The solution must be fault-tolerant. At least once execution of a filter in case of a failure works fine.
item.summary: Asynchronous execution of ContinuousQuery's remote filter & local list

status.description: The issue is considered finished, the resolution is correct. Issues which are not closed can be reopened.

comments.comment:
Folks,

Please note that the problem is much wider than ContinuousQuery. Currently users cannot execute blocking ops in any of our callback, including at least:
1) Futures (listen, chain)
2) Cont. queries
3) Messages.

I think we must split th work into two parts:
1) Create generic solution allowing any callback to be executed in some other thread.
2) Implement failover for cont. queries.

Just wanted to clarify that the same limitation applies to the query listeners (unless the term "filter" is used loosely to also include the listeners): they are invoked synchronously by the same thread that has caused the cache event.

The JCache's cache listener functionality suffers from the same problem since it's implemented on top the CQ feature. Also, CacheEntryListenerConfiguration.isSynchronous() property is not respected by the current implementation: the listeners are invoked synchronously regardless of the value of the property.
Added separate thread pool which used for executing callbacks. If a listener and a filter implements marker interface then they will be submitted in non-system thread pool.

Reviewed, have some comments:

  • the major issue is that if filter is asynchronous then notification code should be called from the same thread which execute filter, otherwise in current implementation starvation is possible
  • please add tests verifying call order filter and listener
  • CacheContinuousQueryAsyncFilterListenerTest should really fail if lsitener and filter are not async
  • in CacheContinuousQueryAsyncFilterListenerTest pelase add check that continous query event for operation executed from listener/fitler is recevied
Also in this ticket will be fixed issue with ordering of invocations remote filters for atomic caches.

Hi Nikolay,

Reviewed, there are some issues:

  • when asynchronous notification is disabled there should not be any overhead comparing to the current implementation, so please avoid unnecessary closures creation in this case
  • we can optimize closure you create for asynchronous notification: let's remove from it fields which do not change, it is possible to use GridDhtAtomicUpdateFuture for synchronozation instead of CountDownLatch
  • for me looks like changes in CacheContinuousQueryHandler.notifyCallback are not necessary, why not just run this method in new pool when asynchronous notification is enabled?
Removed overhead in case when asynchronous notification is disabled. Added test which perform cache operations from callback.

Fixed review notes: removed overhead when async notification is disabled. Optimized closure that using for for asynchronous notification. Used GridDhtAtomicUpdateFuture for synchronozation. Refactored CacheContinuousQueryHandler.notifyCallback method that now using the same code for async and sync notifications. Waiting TC,

Semen,
Could you please review changes from ignite-2004 branch?

Reviewed, my comments:

  • please add failover test with async mode
  • please add test using JCache API + async listener/filter
  • please get rid of unnecessary calls of 'updateListeners' in GridDhtAtomicCache
  • when I change number of threads to 20 in CacheContinuousQueryOperationFromCallbackTest then test fails to wait for some events, please check if this is test issue or cache bug (I want to change test to use 'IgniteConfiguration.systemThreadPoolSize * 2' threads)
  • I see that CacheContinuousQueryOrderingEventTest, CacheContinuousQueryOperationFromCallbackTest use writeSynchronizationMode=PRIMARY_SYNC, let's also add tests with FULL_SYNC

Fixed review notes: added tests using JCache API and async listener/filter, failover test with async, added PRIMARY and FULL_SYNC modes for CacheContinuousQueryOrderingEventTest and CacheContinuousQueryOperationFromCallbackTest tests. Changed thread count for CacheContinuousQueryOperationFromCallbackTest test, now for cache operations are executing from systemThreadPoolSize * 2 threads. Got benchmarks results, no performance drop..

Hi,

I did few very minor changes, please take a look. Please fix javadoc for IgniteAsyncCallback (statement about pools) and for ContinuousQuery (IgniteAsyncCallback is not an interface).

Also please make 'CacheContinuousQueryHandler.notifyCallback' more optimal: do not create any additional collections if all entries are for the same parition. Also I think Collection in this method is always List, so it is possible to avoid iterator creation.

Thank you for your review! I've fixed notes.
